source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Boot to BIOS setup menu
    2. Check the value of System Time in Main page

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Value of System Time should be shown correctly

original_test_intent: Visually verify that the BIOS Main-page System Time tracks the approved RTC/time source within the defined tolerance and display convention.
original_method: Synchronize reference clocks, enter BIOS Setup, record the UI time with a simultaneous timestamp, normalize RTC/local/UTC semantics, calculate offset within the approved tolerance, and exit without editing the clock.
manual_activity: A human must visually record the running BIOS clock at a known instant and ensure no edit occurs; a separately sampled OS clock cannot prove display value or drift.
safety_requirements: Use timestamps close enough to make the tolerance meaningful.
Do not substitute NTP-adjusted OS time without normalization.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare synchronized OS/RTC/BMC samples and offset calculation when later approved.
Report observed offset without claiming UI action or verdict.
engineer_actions: Capture the running BIOS time at the synchronized marker.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Valid only as one OS local-time sample; it lacks timezone/RTC state, capture synchronization and BIOS UI proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Preserve the exact command and pair it with RTC/timezone state plus a synchronized UI frame; do not replace the visual test.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact `date +%T` command, Main-page time check and 10/10-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a timestamped video/frame with a synchronized reference clock, calculate normalized offset and, if required by the plan, observe tick progression without editing.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record OS/NTP/timezone, BIOS, BMC and capture metadata.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Converts 'correct' into a reproducible offset/tolerance comparison.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Unsynchronized screenshots cannot prove a seconds-level tolerance.

project_override_considerations: The project supplies the allowed offset and time convention; the execution report must state them and cannot claim a tighter master criterion than was approved.
expected_evidence: Unchanged clock, normal boot and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets System Time. The missing tolerance/time policy is readiness, not contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The UI-clock objective is clear; project timing semantics and console govern readiness.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the OS command only as a synchronized reference and rejects command-only YES.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on manual UI core and time-policy/tolerance requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Adds explicit offset calculation and project-plan reporting.

review_improvement: Defines how to judge a continuously changing value, avoiding false results from unsynchronized OS/UI samples.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike System Date, this case needs temporal synchronization and tolerance. Automated reference collection helps, but visible running-clock observation remains core, so MANUAL ONLY applies.
no_automatic_retry: Do not edit the clock or repeat setup entry automatically after an offset/timing-evidence problem; preserve samples and stop.
